content: Bākharzī describes a fraught meeting between Jāmī and Sharaf al-Dīn Yazdī on the bank of the Injīl canal after Yazdī moved to Herat, punished by Shāhrukh for his connection with prince Sulṭān-Muḥammad b. Bāysunghur's bid for Iraq (850/1446); MK guesses Jāmī was in his late thirties and Yazdī in his late seventies or early eighties. Yazdī, asked about a Sufi point, replied that he had sworn never again to discuss such matters, because in Shāhrukh's time the jurists had spewed slander against 'this group' (ṭāyifa).
